en: Bodhasūtra 1: “Ask, O Bodha, whatever you desire.
2: “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors does a noble disciple quickly attain the destruction of the outflows (*āsravakṣaya*) in this Dharma and Vinaya?”
“Therefore, Bodha, ask him yourself; then explain it to him as you see fit! What do you think, Bodha?

Are you skilled in your father’s craft and occupations, such as: on the neck of an elephant, on the back of a horse, in a chariot, in archery, in the bow, in retreating, in charging, in handling the goad, in handling the noose, in handling the elephant-hook, and in writing, calculation, accounting, reckoning, and sealing?”

“Truly, Venerable Sir, I am skilled in my father’s craft and occupations, namely: in elephant-riding, horseback riding, charioteering, in the use of the sword, in archery, in retreat, in advance, in the handling of the goad, in the handling of the spear, and in writing, calculation, accounting, arithmetic, and sealing.
“Then suppose a man were to come and think to himself: ‘Ah, Prince Bodha is indeed skilled in his father’s craft and occupations!’”

“Namely: elephant-riding, horseback riding, charioteering, the use of the bow and arrow, retreat, advance, the handling of the goad, the handling of the lasso, the handling of the javelin, writing, calculation, accounting, numeration, and sealing. Suppose I were to learn some particular craft or field of work from him. [The Buddha continued: “And suppose he were to be faithless. What do you think, Bodha: would he obtain that which is to be obtained by one who has faith?”
“No, Venerable Sir. “He might also be deceitful; what do you think, Bodha: would such a deceitful person obtain what is not to be obtained? “No, Venerable Sir.”

Hart_8: “And suppose he were to be beset by much affliction; what do you think, Bodha: would he attain that which is to be attained by one with little affliction? “No, Venerable Sir. Hart_9: “And suppose he were to be lacking in exerted vigor; what do you think, Bodha: would he attain that which is to be attained by one who has exerted vigor?”
“No, Venerable Sir.
“Suppose he were also lacking in wisdom; what do you think, Bodha: would that man obtain what is to be obtained by one who is wise?
“No, Venerable Sir. Even with each of these factors individually, Venerable Sir, it is not easy for that man [to attain it].”
“...to learn from me any one or another craft or field of activity; how much more so all of them!

(Hart 11) “Then a second man might come and think: ‘Oh, Prince Bodha is indeed skilled in his father’s crafts and fields of activity, such as elephant-riding, horseback riding, charioteering, archery, swordsmanship, and retreat!’”

"In exiting [the city], in seizing the hook, in seizing the noose, in seizing the javelin, in writing, counting, and arranging, and in the art of seals—what if I were to learn some particular craft or field of work from him? Suppose he were faithful; what do you think, Bodha, would he obtain that which is to be obtained by one who is faithful?"
“Yes, Venerable Sir.
“And suppose he were free from deceit; what do you think, Bodha: would he attain that which is to be attained by one who is free from deceit?
“Yes, Venerable Sir.”
Hart_14: “Furthermore, he might be free from illness. What do you think, Bodha: would he attain that which is to be attained by one who is free from illness?

“So it is, Venerable Sir. Hart_15: “Furthermore, he might be one who has initiated vigor. What do you think, Bodha: would he attain that which is to be attained by one who has initiated vigor? “So it is, Venerable Sir.”

“Moreover, he might be wise. What do you think, Bodha: would that wise man obtain what ought to be obtained by a wise man? “Yes, Venerable Sir. For, Venerable Sir, if a man were endowed with even one of these qualities, it would be easy for him to acquire from me any one or another of the various crafts or occupations; how much more so if he were endowed with them all!”
Hart_17 “In the same way, Bodha, a noble disciple endowed with five principal factors quickly attains the destruction of the outflows (*āsravakṣaya*) in this Dharma and Vinaya. With which five?

Hart_18.1 Here, Bodha, a noble disciple possesses faith that is firmly established toward the Tathāgata, rooted, grounded, and unshakable by any ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world, in accordance with the Dharma.”
In this way, the noble disciple is endowed with this first essential factor.

Furthermore, O Bodha, the noble disciple becomes free from deceit, free from guile, upright, and of an upright nature; he reveals himself as he truly is before the Teacher and his wise fellow-practitioners. By this second essential factor...
The noble disciple is thus endowed. Furthermore,
the noble disciple is free from much affliction, is by nature healthy, and possesses a digestive faculty that is balanced,
neither too hot nor too cold, untroubled, and pleasant according to the season, by which he properly and comfortably digests whatever he has eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted.
They reach full maturity; by this third essential factor, the noble disciple becomes endowed with it.

Furthermore, O Bodha, the noble disciple dwells with energy aroused, possessing steadfastness, possessing vigor, being enterprising, firm in his resolve, and not casting off the burden regarding wholesome qualities: "Let only skin, sinews, and bones remain, and let my flesh and blood dry up."

From the body comes flesh and blood. Furthermore, that which is to be attained by one who has initiated vigor—one who is steadfast, vigorous, energetic, firm in prowess, and undaunted in his burden regarding wholesome qualities—verily, there shall be no slackening of vigor midway before it is attained.
By this fourth essential factor, the noble disciple becomes endowed.

Furthermore, the noble disciple who possesses wisdom dwells endowed with the wisdom that understands the arising and passing away of the world—the noble, transcendental, penetrative wisdom that leads to deliverance. For what reason? It is for the sake of the complete destruction of suffering and for making an end to suffering.
By this fifth essential factor, the noble disciple becomes fully endowed.
“Bodha, endowed with these five principal factors, the noble disciple quickly attains the destruction of the taints in this Dharma and Discipline.
Then Prince Bodha, uplifting his upper body and extending his right arm, with a mind full of joy, uttered this inspired exclamation:
“O, the Buddha! O, the Dharma! O, the Saṅgha! O, the well-expounded nature of the Dharma, in which now—”
“An noble disciple endowed with these five principal factors will very quickly attain the destruction of the taints in this Dharma and Vinaya!”
